# BUG-002 — validate_date accepts ISO week-date strings (YYYY-Www-D)

**Service:** event-service
**Type:** implementation bug (the spec is correct, the code was not)
**Requirement violated:** REQ-EVT-F03-AC5 (only well-formed `YYYY-MM-DD` strings are valid dates). The contract declares `start_date`/`end_date` as OpenAPI `format: date` (RFC 3339 full-date = `YYYY-MM-DD`).

## Found by

Exploratory testing during the bug-workflow investigation (T-18), targeting the date
validation boundary.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Call `validators.validate_date("2026-W40-1")`.
2. Or `POST /api/v1/events` with `start_date: "2026-W40-1"`.

## Expected behaviour

- `validate_date("2026-W40-1")` -> `False`.
- `POST /api/v1/events` with such a value -> `422 VALIDATION_ERROR`.

## Actual behaviour (before fix)

- `validate_date("2026-W40-1")` -> `True`, and the POST passed validation, because
  `datetime.date.fromisoformat` (Python 3.11+) also parses ISO week dates, which are
  exactly 10 characters long, so the `len(value) == 10` guard did not reject them
  (contradicting the code comment that claimed it accepts exactly `YYYY-MM-DD`).

## Root cause

In `app/validators.py`, `validate_date` only checked that `date.fromisoformat` did not
raise and that `len == 10`, without enforcing the canonical `YYYY-MM-DD` form.

## Fix

After parsing, require the canonical round-trip `parsed.isoformat() == value`, so only a
`YYYY-MM-DD` string (which re-formats to itself) is accepted; ISO week/ordinal forms are
rejected. File: `app/validators.py`.

## Regression tests (fail before the fix, pass after)

`services/event-service/tests/unit/test_regression_bugs.py`
- `test_validate_date_rejects_iso_week_dates` (parametrized: `2026-W40-1`, `2026-W01-7`)
- `test_validate_event_create_rejects_iso_week_date`

## Fix commit

`a418e86` — `fix(event): reject ISO week dates in validate_date, require YYYY-MM-DD [T-18]`
(both fixes were committed together in `a418e86`).
